## Comparability caveat

Alaska Air Group's FY2024 is **not organically comparable** to its FY2022–FY2023 figures. Alaska closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and consolidated Hawaiian's results from that date forward, contributing **$869 million of revenue** in the stub period [DOC-2]. Its headline FY2024 revenue of $11,735M [DOC-1] therefore blends organic and acquired revenue. The other four carriers are all calendar-year filers with no comparable structural change disclosed in these excerpts [DOC-1].

## Growth calculations

| Carrier | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY24 vs FY23 | FY24 vs FY22 (2-yr CAGR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta [DOC-1] | $50,582M | $58,048M | $61,643M | +6.2% | +21.9% (10.4%) |
| United [DOC-1] | $44,955M | $53,717M | $57,063M | +6.2% | +26.9% (12.7%) |
| Southwest [DOC-1] | $23,814M | $26,091M | $27,483M | +5.3% | +15.4% (7.4%) |
| American [DOC-1] | $48,971M | $52,788M | $54,211M | +2.7% | +10.7% (5.2%) |
| Alaska (as reported) [DOC-1] | $9,646M | $10,426M | $11,735M | +12.6% | +21.7% (10.3%) |
| Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) [DOC-1][DOC-2] | $9,646M | $10,426M | ~$10,866M | ~+4.2% | ~+12.7% (6.2%) |

## Assessment

Alaska posts the highest headline FY2024 growth (+12.6%), but stripping out the $869M of acquired Hawaiian revenue [DOC-2] reduces organic growth to roughly +4.2% — below Delta, United, and Southwest.

On an apples-to-apples basis, **United** shows the strongest momentum: it essentially ties Delta on FY2024 year-over-year growth (+6.23% vs. +6.19%) while leading decisively on the two-year stack (+26.9% vs. Delta's +21.9%), reflecting the fastest recovery trajectory off the FY2022 base [DOC-1]. American is the clear laggard at +2.7% year-over-year and +10.7% over two years [DOC-1].

ANSWER: United Airlines Holdings — on an organic, like-for-like basis United had the strongest momentum (+6.2% in FY2024 and +26.9% cumulative since FY2022, a 12.7% two-year CAGR). Alaska's higher headline +12.6% FY2024 growth is not comparable because it includes $869M of revenue from the Hawaiian acquisition consolidated from September 18, 2024; excluding that, Alaska grew only ~4.2%.
